current.text: He is healthy now and not injured.
He is angling for a max contract.
He is a projected starter for Washington. He plays center on offense, and Alex Sarr moves to power forward.
He is projected for about 32 minutes per game.
Davis and Trae Young are expected to get the preferred offensive touches in Washington, ahead of rookie AJ Dybantsa and Alex Sarr.

Experts expect Washington to keep him and push for the playoffs. One is about 80% sure of that. A trade cannot be ruled out, and the team could reconsider around the trade deadline. Golden State has come up in trade rumors.

Washington's rebuild is over. The team is trying to compete, with a projection of about 40 wins and a play-in spot, so late-season rest and minutes cuts are not expected. His health is a key factor for the team.
Washington has only 14 back-to-backs this season and one in the fantasy playoffs.
Experts call his Yahoo rank of about 45 far too late. They value him around picks 23 to 26 and see an early third round pick as an easy call. They see his slide in drafts as an overreaction.
He projects as a top 20 player per game, possibly about 14th. At Yahoo pick 45, that removes most of the injury risk.
ESPN's rank of about 14 is too high to draft him there.
In auctions, one expert values him at 30 USD on a per-game basis but would only buy him at a discount. He went for 26 USD in that mock auction.
Do not expect 75 games. If he plays about 60 games, a pick in the mid 20s is a really good one.
Pairing him with Victor Wembanyama makes blocks and rebounds strong, but the team then needs guard stats.

durable.text: Blocks and rebounds are his standout categories. Both are far above the top 250 pool.

He gets many different injuries, such as shoulder and groin issues and lower body problems. In Dallas he never played five games in a row before getting hurt. There is no single recurring injury like multiple knee surgeries.
Experts have low confidence in his lower body. If he played 62 games, he would be in tier three or four among centers.
He is 33. His outside shooting and perimeter game decline every year, and he now rarely shoots anything except at the rim.
One expert says he can no longer shoot and is now a worse rim protector than Alex Sarr. Another says he can still be productive when he is on the floor.
He is better in category leagues than in points leagues.
As an often-injured player, he is worth a bit less in head-to-head than in roto.

note: Experts say Davis is a top 20 player per game with elite blocks and rebounds and a plus FG%. Their only doubt is how many games he plays, and they set the bar at about 60. Yahoo prices him at 23 USD (average cost 19.1 USD). ESPN prices him at 45 USD, but experts call ESPN's rank too high. One expert gives him 30 USD of per-game value but would only buy at a discount. Our league paid 54 USD last season, so bid into the mid 20s USD and let him go if the room chases him. He fits builds that are strong in BLK, REB and FG%, such as next to Wembanyama, but those builds then need guard stats and threes. Early in the season, check his games played, whether his minutes stay near 32, and any trade talk before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
